subject: SIG: Request for cloud providers, telemetry and support tooling roster
messages:
From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acmecorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — subprocessor roster needed for procurement

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Our procurement and security teams are working through the SIG questionnaire and we need a current roster of Redwood's subprocessors focused on three categories: cloud providers (compute/storage), telemetry/observability (metrics/tracing/logs), and customer support tooling (ticketing/chat).

Can you provide a CSV or table with the following columns: vendor name, product/service, primary region(s), purpose (brief), data categories accessed (e.g., PII, logs, aggregated metrics), and whether the vendor has a subprocessors/sub-subcontractors list? We are on a tight procurement cadence and would appreciate this by EOD Friday (2026-05-21) if possible.

Separately, if you already have a SIG-specific export or an annotated answers PDF for the SIG v3.1, please attach that as well. If there are any items that require an NDA before sharing, let me know.

Best,
Alice Wu
Vendor Risk | Acme Corp
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — subprocessor roster needed for procurement

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. We're pulling the roster together now and will attach a CSV that matches the columns you specified. Quick notes:

- We'll include cloud compute/storage (primary cloud regions), telemetry providers (what telemetry is collected and whether it contains user-identifiable fields), and support tools (ticket/chat systems and data retention policies).
- I've looped in Neha (security/compliance) for any SOC/SIG artifacts and Priyom for vendor contracts and subprocessor details.
- We can send a redacted CSV for public-facing items and a more detailed internal export under a mutual NDA if needed. Is Acme able to accept the standard Redwood data processing addendum (DPA)?

Attached: redwood_subprocessors_20260521.csv (initial export). We'll follow up with an annotated SIG export (PDF) tomorrow morning with a few clarifications.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the CSV stub. A few follow-ups from our side so we can map answers into our vendor risk platform:

1) For Datadog, can you confirm whether traces or logs ever contain user-identifiable information (names, email addresses, account IDs)? If so, which teams/sources ship those traces?
2) For Intercom (and other support tools), do transcripts ever get stored outside a support tool (e.g., exported to S3 or shared with third-party analytics)? If yes, please note retention windows.
3) Can you attach any SOC 2 report date or a completed SIG export (PDF) so we can reconcile control mappings?

If you can send short clarifications inline in the CSV or as a supplemental PDF that would be ideal. Thanks — we just need this for the risk committee today.

Best,
Alice

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — subprocessor roster needed for procurement

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clarifying questions. Quick answers below and attached an updated CSV plus a brief SIG export PDF: sig-completed-answers.pdf. I've bolded the short answers in the PDF for the risk committee.

1) Datadog: traces forwarded to Datadog are application-generated and do not include customer PII by design. We redact user-identifiable fields at the instrumentation layer for PII (email, full name). Account IDs used for routing are internal opaque IDs and not customer-facing identifiers.

2) Intercom: transcripts live in Intercom by default and are retained per our support retention policy (90 days for chats, 2 years for ticket attachments). We do not routinely export transcripts to S3; exports happen only for engineering investigations and are time-limited and access controlled. When exports occur they are stored in AWS S3 with server-side encryption and 30-day retention unless otherwise requested.

3) SOC 2: our latest SOC 2 report (Type II) covers the period 2025-06-01 to 2026-05-31. We can provide the auditor letter under NDA.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20260522.csv (updated with retention and PII flags), sig-completed-answers.pdf (annotated SIG mapping). Also uploaded to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSharedFolder

If the committee wants any follow-up evidence (config screenshots, retention policy excerpts), Neha can provide those. Neha — can you prepare a short bundle for Acme if they request it?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
